title: Work Today
description: Ten short stories, e-mails, diary entries and reports about work today: working from home, an office kitchen, a new manager, a startup's rules for evenings, a design convention, a career change at 50, lunchtime basketball, a colleague expecting twins, a family store and a lunchtime chess club.

lessons.title: Working from Home
lessons.summary: A mother starts working from home three days a week and learns to plan her day while her son builds a fort.
lessons.text:
Monday, March 3

Today was my first day of working from home. Our team is small, and from now on we will be working from home 3 days a week. Normally, I take the train to the office at 7:30. This morning, I made coffee and sat down at my desk at 8:00. It felt strange, but I liked it.

My desk is in a small room that we used for storage. Last week, I moved all the storage boxes into the garage, and I put a desk, a lamp and a plant in the room. It is not big, but it is quiet.

At 9:00, we had our weekly team meeting on video. Every Monday, our manager, Karen, tells us the top priority for the week. This week, the top priority is a new website for a client. Karen showed us her slides. On the last slide, she had written: "Ask questions!" She said, "If anybody has a problem, write in the team thread. Don't wait for the next weekly meeting." Then she said, "Anybody can write in the thread at any time."

Wednesday, March 5

Working from home is harder than I expected. My son, Sam, is 6, and he had no school today. While I was answering messages in the team thread, he made a fort out of the old storage boxes in the garage. Every 10 minutes, he ran into my room and said, "Mom, come into my fort!" I told him, "I can't play now. I'm working." He looked sad. I should have planned the day better. If I had asked my mother to come, Sam would have had someone to play with.

Friday, March 7

Today I made a plan. Normally, I answer messages all day, but now I check the thread only 3 times a day: at 9, at 12 and at 4. My first priority every morning is the most difficult work. Between 12 and 1, I have lunch with Sam, and sometimes I visit his fort. He says it is the best fort in the world.

By the end of next week, I will have finished my part of the website. Hopefully, Karen will like it. And hopefully, Sam will be back at school!

Questions:
How many days a week will the team be working from home?
They will be working from home 3 days a week.
What did the mother use the small room for before?
She used it for storage.
What does Karen tell the team at the weekly meeting?
She tells them the top priority for the week.
Where should anybody with a problem write?
They should write in the team thread.
What did Sam make out of the storage boxes?
He made a fort.
How did the mother change her day?
She checks the thread only 3 times a day, and the most difficult work is her first priority every morning.

lessons.title: The Office Kitchen
lessons.summary: An office manager writes to everyone about dirty cups and a wet floor in the kitchen, and gives some simple instructions.
lessons.text:
Subject: Our office kitchen

Hi everyone,

I'm writing about our office kitchen. As you know, we are a small company, and we don't have anybody to clean the kitchen during the day. So we all have to help.

Over the last 2 weeks, I have received 5 complaints about the kitchen. Most of the complaints were about dirty cups. On Friday afternoon, I counted 2 dozen dirty cups in the sink. That's 24 cups! By Monday morning, the sink smelled bad, and there were no clean cups left. Someone must have left the water running, too, because the floor in front of the sink was wet.

The wet floor was the most serious problem. On Monday morning, Tom slipped on the wet floor and fell. Luckily, he was not hurt. "No harm done," he told me. But if he had hit his head, there could have been real harm. I don't want anybody else to slip in our kitchen.

So here are 4 simple instructions:

1. Wash your cup and put it away. Please don't leave dirty cups in the sink.
2. If you see water on the floor, clean it up right away. It is very easy to slip on a wet floor.
3. Put your food in the fridge in a box with your name on it.
4. Every Friday at 5, all food without a name will be thrown away.

I have printed these instructions and put them on the wall next to the sink. Personally, I don't enjoy writing e-mails like this one. I would much rather write about birthday cakes! But I think the instructions will help, and they will only take you a minute a day.

I have also ordered another dozen cups, so there will be enough cups for everyone.

If you have any other complaints or ideas, please come and talk to me personally. My door is always open.

Thank you,
Linda

Questions:
How many complaints has Linda received?
She has received 5 complaints.
What were most of the complaints about?
Most of the complaints were about dirty cups.
How many dirty cups were in the sink on Friday?
There were 2 dozen dirty cups in the sink, which is 24 cups.
What happened to Tom on Monday?
He slipped on the wet floor and fell, but he was not hurt.
Where did Linda put the instructions?
She put them on the wall next to the sink.
Why did Linda order another dozen cups?
She ordered them so that there would be enough cups for everyone.

lessons.title: The New Manager
lessons.summary: Ben's new manager defines his role clearly, explains her expectations and gives him tips after a mistake.
lessons.text:
Ben has worked at a small software company for 4 years. Last month, his old manager left, and a new manager, Rosa, joined the team. Ben was a little nervous. His old manager had been kind, but he had never explained his expectations, so Ben often didn't know what he was supposed to do.

On her first day, Rosa had a meeting with each person on the team. Unlike the old manager, she brought a notebook and wrote everything down. "I want to define everyone's role clearly," she told Ben. "When a role is clearly defined, people know what to do, and they don't waste time. So how would you define your job?"

Ben thought for a moment. "I suppose I have 2 jobs," he said. "I fix problems in our app, and I answer questions from our clients."

"Which do you enjoy more?" Rosa asked.

"The latter," Ben said. "I really like talking to clients."

"Good," Rosa said. "We need someone who likes clients. Let's make the latter your main job."

Then Rosa told Ben her 3 expectations. First, every report must be accurate. Second, if a task is going to be late, he should tell her early. Third, he should confirm every client meeting by e-mail the day before. "Those are my only expectations," she said. "They are simple, but they are important."

Two weeks later, Ben sent Rosa a report about the clients' questions. Rosa found a mistake in it: some of the numbers were not accurate. Ben felt terrible. He wished he had checked the report before he sent it. "If I had checked the numbers, I would have seen the mistake," he said. "I suppose I was in a hurry."

"Everyone makes mistakes," Rosa said. "Here are some tips. Check every number twice. Then ask a colleague to read the report. And never write a report in a hurry." Ben wrote the tips down and put them on his desk.

His next report was accurate. Rosa read it and smiled. "This is exactly what I wanted," she said. Ben also started confirming every client meeting the day before, and the clients liked it. Now that his role was clearly defined, Ben knew exactly what his job was. Unlike before, he enjoyed going to work every morning.

Questions:
Why was Ben nervous?
He was nervous because his old manager had never explained his expectations.
How was Rosa different from the old manager?
Unlike the old manager, she brought a notebook and wrote everything down.
Which of his 2 jobs does Ben enjoy more?
He enjoys the latter more: talking to clients.
What were Rosa's 3 expectations?
Reports must be accurate, Ben should tell her early if a task is going to be late, and he should confirm every client meeting by e-mail.
What tips did Rosa give Ben?
She told him to check every number twice, to ask a colleague to read the report and never to write a report in a hurry.

lessons.title: An Amendment for Evenings
lessons.summary: A small startup adds an amendment to its one-page constitution so that people can rest in the evenings.
lessons.text:
When Maya and her friend Josh started their company 3 years ago, there were only 2 of them. Now there are 14 people, and the company is still growing. Last year, Maya decided that the team needed a short document about how they work together. She called it "our constitution."

The constitution is only one page long. It says that everyone in the company is dedicated to good work, that people help each other and that every voice matters. The whole team wrote it together, and everyone signed it.

However, after a few months, Maya noticed a problem. People were frequently sending messages late at night and on weekends, and others were frequently answering them. Many people were tired, and 2 people told Maya that they never really stopped working.

So Maya suggested an amendment to the constitution. The amendment said: "Nobody has to answer work messages after 7 in the evening or on weekends."

Not everyone liked the amendment. There was some opposition, especially from Josh. "We are a small startup," he said. "Our clients frequently need fast answers. If we stop answering at 7, we might lose them." A few other people agreed with him. Maya listened to the opposition carefully. She understood the importance of clients, but she also understood the importance of rest.

The team discussed the amendment for 2 weeks. Ultimately, they added one sentence to it: "Depending on the project, one person may answer clients in the evening. This person will change every week, depending on who is free." After that, the opposition disappeared, and the team voted for the amendment. Even Josh voted for it.

For most people, the amendment was a great relief. They started to rest in the evenings. Instead of checking their phones, they spent time with their families and friends. "What a relief," said Lily, who works on the company's app. "Now I can close my laptop at 7 and not think about work."

The company did not lose any clients. Ultimately, the team is working better, because people are rested. "I'm dedicated to this company," Josh said a few months later, "but I'm also dedicated to my family. I should have supported the amendment from the beginning."

Questions:
What did Maya call the short document?
She called it "our constitution."
What problem did Maya notice?
People were frequently sending messages late at night and on weekends.
What did the amendment say?
It said that nobody has to answer work messages after 7 in the evening or on weekends.
Why was there opposition to the amendment?
Some people, especially Josh, thought that the company might lose clients.
What did the team ultimately add to the amendment?
They added that, depending on the project, one person may answer clients in the evening.
Why was the amendment a relief?
It was a relief because people could rest in the evenings and spend time with their families.

lessons.title: Report from the Convention
lessons.summary: A visual designer writes to her manager about a design convention and a company that wants an exclusive partnership.
lessons.text:
Subject: Report from the design convention

Hi Daniel,

I'm writing from my hotel. The design convention ended this afternoon, and I want to tell you about it before I fly home tomorrow.

The convention was huge. More than 5,000 designers came from 60 countries, so it was a truly worldwide event. There were talks, workshops and hundreds of companies showing their products. As a visual designer, I went to most of the talks about visual design: colors, pictures and how to capture people's attention on a small screen.

The best talk was given by a young designer from Brazil. She said that a good app has to capture a user's attention in the first 3 seconds. If it doesn't capture their attention, they will close it and never open it again. Her examples were brilliant, and I took a lot of notes. I'll share them with the team next week.

On the second day, I met 2 people from Florana, a company that sells plants online. They already have customers worldwide, and next year they are planning an expansion into the United States. For this expansion, they need a partner who can design and build their new app. They had looked at our work online, and they are interested in a partnership with us.

They also offered us an exclusive deal. "Exclusive" means that for 2 years, we would be their only app designer in the United States, and they could not work with any other design company here. As you know, our market is very competitive, and small companies like ours have to fight for every client. An exclusive partnership with a growing company would help us a lot. Their prices also seem competitive.

I told them that I would be happy to discuss the partnership, but that you would make the final decision. They will be calling you on Tuesday. I think their idea is brilliant, but of course we should read the contract carefully first.

By Friday, I will have written a full report about the convention for the whole team.

See you soon,
Sara

Questions:
How many designers came to the convention?
More than 5,000 designers came from 60 countries.
What did the young designer from Brazil say?
She said that a good app has to capture a user's attention in the first 3 seconds.
What is Florana planning for next year?
It is planning an expansion into the United States.
What does an exclusive deal mean here?
It means that for 2 years, Sara's company would be Florana's only app designer in the United States.
Why would the partnership help Sara's company?
Because the market is very competitive, and small companies have to fight for every client.
When will the people from Florana be calling Daniel?
They will be calling him on Tuesday.

lessons.title: A New Career at 50
lessons.summary: After 28 years as a machine operator, Frank goes back to school at 50 and finds work in tourism.
lessons.text:
My name is Frank, and I am 51 years old. For 28 years, I worked in manufacturing. I was a machine operator in a factory that made parts for cars. An operator has to be careful and patient, and I was good at my job. I had a permanent contract, a good salary and friendly colleagues.

However, I always had another dream. I love the history of my city, and I love talking to people. Whenever friends visited us, I showed them around the old town. "You should work in tourism," my wife used to say. But we had 2 children, a house and a permanent job, so I never tried.

Last year, the factory decided to reduce its personnel. The personnel office offered money to any worker who agreed to leave early. Most operators wanted to stay, but I decided to take the money. I was 50, and I thought, "If I don't pursue my dream now, I will never pursue it."

First, I went to the employment office in town. A woman there looked at my past employment and asked me what I wanted to do. When I said "tourism," she did not laugh. She told me about a one-year tourism program at the community college. "Many people change careers at your age," she said.

In September, I started classes. The college campus was full of young people, and I was the oldest student by 30 years. At first, I felt out of place on campus. There was a big gap between me and the other students. They knew everything about computers, and I knew almost nothing. But I knew a lot about my city, and I had worked for 28 years. Slowly, the gap became smaller. The young students helped me with computers, and I helped them with history.

After the program, I found employment with a small tourism company. Now I lead walking tours of the old town 5 days a week. The job is not permanent yet, but I hope it will be soon.

Sometimes I wish I had pursued this dream earlier. But I don't regret my years in manufacturing. They taught me to be patient and careful, and those things help me every day on my tours.

Questions:
What did Frank do for 28 years?
He worked in manufacturing as a machine operator.
What was Frank's dream?
His dream was to work in tourism.
Why did the personnel office offer money to workers?
Because the factory decided to reduce its personnel.
Where did Frank go first?
He went to the employment office in town.
Why did Frank feel out of place on campus?
He was the oldest student, and there was a big gap between him and the other students.
What does Frank do now?
He leads walking tours of the old town 5 days a week.

lessons.title: The Lunch Gang
lessons.summary: A group of colleagues plays basketball at lunch; Jess hurts her knee, rests, and comes back to play.
lessons.text:
Every Wednesday at noon, 8 people from Jess's office walk to the park and play basketball for 45 minutes. They call themselves "the lunch gang." The gang has designers, programmers, a manager and Jess, who works in sales.

Before each game, they throw a coin into the air to decide which team gets the ball first. Tom always throws the coin, because it is his lucky coin.

Last Wednesday, the game was fast and competitive. In the first 10 minutes, the ball hit Mike on the nose. His nose was red, but it was fine, and he kept playing. "My nose is OK," he said, laughing. "It's not the first time."

Twenty minutes later, Jess jumped for the ball and landed badly. She felt a sharp pain in her left knee and sat down on the ground. The whole gang ran to her. "Can you move your knee?" Mike asked. She could move it, but it hurt.

Tom drove her to a doctor near the office. The doctor looked at her knee carefully. "Good news," he said. "The injury isn't severe. But if you had kept playing, it might have become severe. You should rest your knee for 2 weeks."

Back at the office, her colleagues brought her some ice. "We play hard," Tom said. "With 8 people and one ball, someone was bound to get hurt sooner or later. It was only a question of time." Jess smiled and said, "Next time, it's bound to be you!"

Jess missed 2 games, but she still came to the park every Wednesday and watched. "She's a real fighter," Mike said. "Even with a bad knee, she won't stay away from basketball." After 2 weeks, the doctor said her knee was fine, and Jess played again. That day, she scored 6 points, and her team won.

To celebrate, Tom brought a big bottle of cold fruit punch to the park. The gang sat on the grass and drank the punch together. "To Jess, our fighter!" Tom said.

Questions:
What does the lunch gang do every Wednesday?
They play basketball in the park for 45 minutes.
Why does Tom throw a coin before each game?
He throws a coin to decide which team gets the ball first.
What happened to Mike's nose?
The ball hit him on the nose, but it was fine.
What did the doctor say about Jess's knee?
The doctor said the injury wasn't severe, but she should rest her knee for 2 weeks.
Why did Mike call Jess a fighter?
Because she still came to the park and watched, even with a bad knee.
What did Tom bring to celebrate?
He brought a big bottle of cold fruit punch.

lessons.title: Good News from Emma
lessons.summary: Emma tells her remote team that she is expecting twins, and the team sends a baby swing.
lessons.text:
Emma is a programmer at a small company. The company has no office, so the whole team works from home. Emma lives in a small town, and her 5 colleagues live in 4 different countries. They meet on video every Monday.

One Monday in April, at the end of the weekly meeting, Emma said she had some news. "I'm pregnant," she said. "And it's twins!" Everyone smiled and clapped. Her manager, Paul, said, "That's wonderful news, Emma!" Emma said that she was full of joy, but also a little nervous. "Two babies at once!" she said. "I suppose I won't be sleeping much next year."

"Are there any other twins in your family?" Paul asked.

"Yes," Emma said. "My mother is a twin, and so is my grandfather. My doctor says that twins sometimes run in families, and that genes can play a role. So maybe it's in our genes."

After the meeting, Paul called Emma to talk about her plans. "You will have 6 months of leave," he said. "After that, you can work part-time for a year, if you want. Many companies lose good people when they become parents. We want to retain our people, and we really want to retain you."

The team wanted to send Emma a gift. They chose a baby swing: a small seat that moves slowly from side to side and helps babies fall asleep. Paul ordered the swing online, and the store wrapped it in bright yellow paper. Inside the box, there was also a card from the whole team. When the box arrived, Emma took off the wrapping paper and found the swing and the card. She sent the team a photo of the swing.

In October, the twins were born: a boy and a girl. A week later, Emma made an online gallery of baby photos and shared it with the team. The gallery had 30 photos. In many of them, the twins were sleeping in the swing. There was also a short video in the gallery. In it, Emma's husband was singing a quiet tune while the babies slept. It was an old tune that his mother used to sing to him.

"Every photo is full of joy," Paul wrote in the team thread. Everyone agreed.

Questions:
What news did Emma share at the end of the weekly meeting?
She said that she was pregnant with twins.
Who else in Emma's family is a twin?
Her mother and her grandfather are twins.
What did Paul say about retaining people?
He said that the company wants to retain its people, and that it really wants to retain Emma.
What gift did the team send?
They sent a baby swing wrapped in bright yellow paper.
What was in the online gallery?
There were 30 baby photos and a short video.
What was Emma's husband doing in the video?
He was singing a quiet tune while the babies slept.

lessons.title: A Store with a Long History
lessons.summary: A short report about a family jewelry store that a young clerk opened in 1935 and his granddaughter runs today.
lessons.text:
Hart's Jewelry is a small store on Main Street. It sells rings, watches and diamonds, and it has been open for more than 90 years. Today, it is run by Lucy Hart, the granddaughter of the man who started it.

The story began in 1935, during the Great Depression. Times were hard, and millions of people had lost their jobs. Lucy's grandfather, George Hart, was a young clerk in a big retail store in the city. When the store closed during the Depression, George lost his job, too. With very little money, he opened a small shop where he repaired watches.

During the Second World War, George joined the navy. He served for 4 years and became a lieutenant. After the war, he left the navy and went back to his shop. He began to sell rings, and a few years later, diamonds.

Over the years, the business grew. By 1970, George had 3 stores: one in the city and 2 in the surrounding towns. People joked that he was building a jewelry empire. But George did not want an empire. "I just want to sell good things at fair prices," he used to say.

Today, retail is not easy for small stores, because many people shop online. Lucy closed the stores in the surrounding towns and kept only the first one on Main Street. Luckily, Main Street has good public transportation, so customers can come by bus or train. "Public transportation brings us a lot of customers," Lucy says. "Many of them don't even have a car."

Lucy started working as a clerk in the store when she was 16. "My grandfather taught me everything," she says. "He always told me, 'A good clerk listens more than she talks.'" Her most popular product is a small diamond ring. "Young couples are often nervous, because diamonds are expensive," she says. "I tell them that the size of the diamond is not important."

On the wall behind the counter, there is a photo of George in his navy uniform. "He was a lieutenant, and he ran this store like a ship," Lucy says with a smile. "Everything had to be clean and in order." She has no plans to build an empire. "One store is enough," she says. "I think my grandfather would have agreed."

Questions:
When did the story of Hart's Jewelry begin?
It began in 1935, during the Great Depression.
What was George Hart's job before he opened his shop?
He was a young clerk in a big retail store in the city.
What did George become in the navy?
He became a lieutenant.
How many stores did George have by 1970?
He had 3 stores: one in the city and 2 in the surrounding towns.
Why is public transportation important for the store?
Because it brings a lot of customers, and many of them don't have a car.
What is Lucy's most popular product?
Her most popular product is a small diamond ring.

lessons.title: The Lunchtime Chess Club
lessons.summary: A young employee stops eating lunch at her desk when a Greek colleague invites her to a chess club.
lessons.text:
When I started my job at a small travel company last year, I always ate lunch at my desk. I usually ate quickly while I answered messages. Then, one day, my colleague Nikos came to talk to me. Nikos is Greek, and he moved here from Athens 2 years ago.

"In my family, eating lunch at your desk is a sin," he said with a smile. "Come with me, Anna. We're starting a chess club."

I had played chess as a child, but I had forgotten most of the rules. In a small meeting room, there were 3 chess boards on the table and 4 people. Nikos made a cup of strong Greek coffee, and steam was rising from his cup. "Chess is how I let off steam," he said. "When work is hard, I need something that makes me forget about it for an hour."

My first game was against Nikos. I had difficulty remembering how each piece moves. "The bishop moves only on its own color," Nikos explained. "So one bishop always stays on the white squares, and the other bishop always stays on the black squares." I lost both of my bishops in the first 10 minutes. I lost the game, too.

The next week, Nikos did something amazing: he played 3 games in parallel. He walked from board to board and made a move on each one. Even with 3 games in parallel, he won all of them.

I enjoyed the club more than I had expected. Chess reminded me of the fantasy books that I loved as a child, with kings, queens and castles. In a fantasy book, you just read about the battle. In chess, you are the one who plans it.

Slowly, I had less difficulty with the game. I began to think for a long time before every move. "That was a wise move," Nikos said one day, when I moved my bishop to protect my queen. "A wise player always thinks 3 moves ahead."

Now our club has 8 members, and we meet every Tuesday and Thursday. I never eat lunch at my desk anymore. Nikos was right: it really is a sin to work through lunch. After an hour of chess, I go back to my desk calm and full of energy. Last Thursday, I won my first game against Nikos. "I wish I had joined the club a year earlier," I told him. He laughed and said, "Better late than never."

Questions:
Where did Anna eat lunch when she started her job?
She always ate lunch at her desk.
What did Nikos say about eating lunch at your desk?
He said that in his family, eating lunch at your desk is a sin.
Why does Nikos play chess?
Chess is how he lets off steam when work is hard.
How does the bishop move?
The bishop moves only on its own color.
What did Nikos do the next week?
He played 3 games in parallel and won all of them.
What did the chess club remind Anna of?
It reminded her of the fantasy books that she loved as a child.
